title: Jessica Howard named 2027 Iowa Teacher of the Year at Lone Tree Community School District
text:
Jessica Howard named 2027 Iowa Teacher of the Year at Lone Tree Community School District
By D. A. Aranda
Jessica Howard, a business and computer science teacher at Lone Tree Community School District, was named the 2027 Iowa Teacher of the Year during a surprise assembly, according to an announcement on Sep. 16 by Iowa Department of Education Director McKenzie Snow and Lt. Governor Chris Cournoyer on behalf of Governor Kim Reynolds.
Howard has taught for ten years after switching from a career in industry to education, bringing more than a decade of business experience into her classroom. Governor Reynolds said, “Jessica Howard goes beyond teaching content by helping students become solution-oriented, active problem solvers, and that’s exactly how we prepare the next generation with durable skills that will serve them long after graduation. She uses hands-on learning to prepare students to succeed in Iowa’s high-demand, high-skill and high-wage jobs, teaching from a place of real-world experience. This is what exceptional teaching looks like, and I am grateful for teachers like Jessica who help prepare Iowa students for success.”
The Iowa Teacher of the Year award recognizes teachers who demonstrate excellence in the classroom and make significant impacts on student outcomes and their colleagues. Howard was selected from nine finalists recently named as Regional Teachers of the Year across all state education regions; she also serves as Grant Wood Regional Teacher of the Year.
Iowa Department of Education Director McKenzie Snow said, “Jessica, who changed careers from business to education a decade ago, knows firsthand the importance of empowering all learners with multiple pathways to postsecondary success... Nearly 60% of students are attaining a work-based learning experience while in high school. Every day, Jessica works as an education entrepreneur to change lives, empower her community and strengthen her local economy.”
Howard said about her approach, “My approach to teaching... is to make it real-life focused. If I am teaching something, it has to have real-life implications that prepare students for the world they are going to live and work in. I see my students as capable... members of our community...” She also supports students through roles such as concurrent enrollment instructor with Kirkwood Community College; adviser for National Honor Society and Business Professionals of America chapters; coach for Lone Tree’s state champion esports team; participant in work-based learning educator pipeline programs; recipient of grants supporting computer science endorsements; former private sector employee at Lee Enterprises and U.S. Cellular; former STEM award recipient; participant in externship programs pairing educators with local businesses.
In addition to Howard’s recognition this year were regional finalists Ashley Cardamone (Cedar Falls), Tracy Madsen (Central Lee), Lynne Glackin (Woodbine), Jana Dewhurst (Johnston), Tera Bunn (Oelwein), Mitchel Dierickx (Davenport), Roselyn Schillerstrom (West Lyon), Abby Goodlaxson (Okoboji). The annual program began in 1958 through an appropriation from the Iowa Legislature.
